C01.signature: Volunteer elicits duration, acceptable windows and equipment, then compares compatible room-time assignments with inherited bookings. Better matching can admit excluded needs; saturated compatible windows can prevent gains. Preserve minima, performances and C1-C4; implementation requires accurate reports and consent.
C01.reason: Each member supplies requirements-based matching and a compatibility discriminator, even when phrased as a question. Same-time room substitution restricts the assignment choices without changing this path. Minimum protection is shared; no member requires duration reduction as the sole source of gain. H4-F04 supplies reassignment and H4-F05 its demand-map test. Cyclic exchange distinctness remains uncertain; no bridge merge is made.

C02.signature: Volunteer and desk record changes in one authoritative ledger before confirming room/date/time, update derived copies and consult current reservations at access. Aligned records should reduce attributable conflicting expectations; matching-record conflicts and added workload can defeat benefit. Requires consistent use through existing channels.
C02.reason: All fifteen members align authoritative state and confirmation, with conflict or discrepancy tracking. IDs, readback, supersession, timestamps and key checks implement the same path. H4-F01 matches the intervention; H4-F06 matches comparison of changes, confirmations and incident explanations. The diagnostic match does not assert all conflicts have the same cause.

C03.signature: Volunteer allocates requested weekly 60-minute entitlements before optional extensions instead of inheriting 90-minute blocks. Useful shorter durations may free contiguous compatible time for excluded groups while preserving longer actual needs and C1-C4; beneficial shortening and suitable fragments must exist.
C03.reason: P009 A2 explicitly changes duration priority to recover stranded useful time, matching H4-F02. This discriminator differs from finding another compatible room or window in C01. Its requirements intake is a feasibility condition, not evidence that all matching proposals share its duration-dependent cause.

C04.signature: Volunteer compares identical demand under inherited allocation, compatibility matching alone, minimum-plus-extension allocation alone, and both. The combined schedule may improve fulfilled needs beyond either component while protecting minima and performances. Requires useful alternatives and durations; reject violating schedules.
C04.reason: Both members test the interaction of compatibility and duration/entitlement allocation against separate components. H4-F02 and H4-F04 supply operations; H4-F05 supplies the explicitly elicited demand map. The joint discriminator is locally absent from the incomplete archive. Agreed speculative support and bounded-probe fit remain; actual feasibility and outcome are untested.

C05.signature: Volunteer discovers compatible exchanges, retains original reservations until every affected contact consents, then commits all replacements together in the authoritative ledger and confirms access. This should improve allocation without partial or duplicate active rights. Requires reciprocal alternatives, consent and reliable ledger consultation within C1-C4.
C05.reason: P002 A1 and P010 A2 specify the same all-consent commit boundary and retained-original invariant; two versus several groups changes scale. P002 adds component replay and interrupted-handoff tests; P010 tests one swap against a direct change. The concrete operation supports mechanism kind despite speculative benefit. Preserve agreed local novelty; neither establishes world success.

C06.signature: Contacts identify indispensable-player overlap between groups; volunteer compares overlapping obligations with late/missed versus attended sessions and tests accepted staggering or exchanges. Removing supported clashes could improve usable attendance without adding room capacity. Shared membership, necessity, recall and feasible alternatives remain unmeasured.
C06.reason: Unchanged agreed anchor family: all four members specify shared essential attendance as the dependency and overlap-linked failures as its discriminator. H4-F06 supplies only the broader incident investigation. The partial broker wording does not establish a full operating capability or eight-week result.

C07.signature: Volunteer seeks a fully consented cycle of linked booking moves that admits an unmet requirement beyond free-slot allocation or direct swaps, with no loss of protected or required access. Originals remain until agreement; record additional usable access and all coordination effort within C1-C4.
C07.reason: Unchanged agreed anchor family and uncertain novelty. Both members test dependent exchanges beyond simpler moves, but ordinary global compatible reassignment in H4-F04/C01 may already realize those schedules. Their common cycle signature is coherent; separate-family status remains provisional. Failed bounded search cannot establish absence of all useful cycles.

C08.signature: Volunteer matches released slots to preauthorized acceptable replacements and commits reassignment through one ledger. Compare queue-only, ledger-only and combined rules on accepted placements, conflicting confirmations and handling time. Confirm replacement before releasing a weekly minimum; protect C1-C4.
C08.reason: Unchanged agreed singleton: archived release/queue and authoritative-record components are crossed at change commitment, with an explicit joint-versus-components prediction. It concerns released-slot placement rather than simultaneous reciprocal exchange. Preauthorization, handling savings and outcomes remain untested.
